ISA version 0.1. Contract: `doc/phase1_tasks_and_acceptance.md` R1-01.

Four columns, because they disagree. An instruction can be in the ISA
and in no profile; in a profile and beyond the compiler; emitted by the
compiler and never executed on the whole machine. One word --
"supported" -- hides all three differences, which is what the audit
found. None of these columns is written by hand: each is derived from
the normative ISA export, the generated target descriptions, the
lowering itself, and the programs `make top` runs.

"machine verified" means the mnemonic is executed by a program running
on the four-tile machine (`make top`: `t10_mesh`, `t24_amo_mesh`).
A `no` there is not a defect -- most instructions are verified on the
single-core bench, which `make core` runs under three memory models --
it is a statement about which column of evidence exists.

is false everywhere, so asking for it is a compile error rather than a
runtime trap. Calling that either "yes" or "no" would say something
false about it.

## Limits

| what | limit | where it is enforced |
|---|---|---|
| dtype (matrix) | f16, bf16, e5m2, e4m3 | compiler/python/tnca_cc/footprints.py `MMA_DTYPE_BITS`; an unknown dtype is a Diagnostic, checked by FP-05 |
| dtype (transfer) | f16, bf16, f32 | the element-size suffix in `_lower_transfer`; anything else has no suffix and cannot be emitted |
| dtype (convert) | f32, bf16, f16, e5m2, e4m3 | `vf.cvt.<src>.<dst>` mod[5:0], ISA sec 8.4; t21_cvt runs all twenty-five source/destination pairs, sixteen lanes each |
| K step | k16, k32, k64 | `MMA_K_STEPS`; the footprint is sized from the INSTRUCTION, which is audit F01 and case FP-02/FP-04 |
| output tile | at most the accumulator shape (16x16) | `plan_gemm` refuses a larger tile; a bigger output needs several accumulators and an outer loop, which is not planned |
| transfer rank | 1 to 5 | ISA sec 9E (R38): signed coordinates, out-of-bounds elements zero- or NaN-filled on a load and not written by a store; rank > 5 raises DESCRIPTOR_FAULT. tb/core/progs/t33_tdesc_load.s, t34_tdesc_store.s |
| transfer stride | innermost stride = element size; base, outer strides and coordinates any alignment | an unaligned row is assembled from two memory words per unit (rtl/core/tnca_tensor.v); t17_descfault is the negative for a non-contiguous innermost stride |
| window write granularity | whole 8-byte units, rows a multiple of 8 bytes | a box row whose size is not a whole number of 8-byte units raises DESCRIPTOR_FAULT; partial units at a tensor edge are filled per the padding mode through the byte keep-mask |
| control flow | a single block per region; loops via `b.loop` | multi-block CFG, nested regions and events through block arguments are refused by name -- IR-02. This is a frozen boundary, not a removed capability |
| async lifetime | one completion event per command; sources release on command completion | ISA v0.1 `source_release`; the compiler takes the bound rather than the looser one sec 10.2 permits hardware |

## Asynchronous operations

For each: what the engine reads and writes beyond the registers the
encoding names, when the resource is held, what releases it, what an
error completion does, how it counts against a barrier generation, and
what happens when it is predicated off. These are the facts
`compiler_overview.md` sec 13.4 says must be in the compiler model,
because a liveness analysis built from the operand fields sees two
registers where the engine touches thirty-two.

### `t.ld.async`

- **reads** the coordinate run: `rank` consecutive scalars from Sb (ISA sec 9E), plus the descriptor snapshot
- **writes** the whole destination window, every register of it
- **held** the window, from issue
- **released by** the completion event; the coordinate registers are free one cycle after issue, because rtl/core/tnca_tensor.v latches c0..c4 on cmd_valid and never reads the file again (case OWN-04)
- **on error** the barrier is signalled with its error bit set, so the waiter is released rather than hanging; the window is not published
- **barrier generation** counts one operation on the armed phase of its barrier
- **predicated off** a fully masked-off transfer performs no access and still completes exactly once (ISA sec 9A.3), so the static operation count stays correct (case OWN-09)

### `t.st.async`

- **reads** the source window -- LATE, after the issuing instruction has retired (sec 13.4) -- and the coordinate run
- **writes** memory only; no register file
- **held** the source window, from issue
- **released by** the completion event. Reading the window meanwhile is legal; overwriting it is not (case OWN-03)
- **on error** a refused geometry raises DESCRIPTOR_FAULT with the barrier error bit set, so the waiter is released (t35_tdesc_fpad2)
- **barrier generation** counts one operation on the armed phase of its barrier
- **predicated off** a fully masked-off transfer performs no access and still completes exactly once (ISA sec 9A.3)

### `m.mma.async`

- **reads** both fragments in full: fragment_registers(m,k) and fragment_registers(k,n) from the INSTRUCTION's K and dtype, not the target default (audit F01)
- **writes** the destination accumulator, for the whole command
- **held** both source windows and the accumulator, from issue
- **released by** the completion event. With mod[4] the source-free event arrives one barrier phase earlier; on ISA v0.1 the compiler takes command completion for both
- **on error** the barrier carries the error bit; the accumulator is left undefined and must not be read
- **barrier generation** counts one operation, or two with the source-free event, on the armed phase
- **predicated off** the same rule: completes once, whatever the mask

### `t.prefetch`

- **reads** the coordinate run
- **writes** nothing architectural
- **held** nothing
- **released by** none: it raises no completion and counts on no barrier
- **on error** none; a failed prefetch is not observable
- **barrier generation** n/a -- it must never be counted in an mb.arm
- **predicated off** performs no access when masked off, like any other

## Not delivered

Listed because R1-01 forbids marking an undelivered requirement as not
applicable. Each of these is a FAIL or NOT RUN, never an absence.

| item | status | where it is tracked |
|---|---|---|
| a box row that is not a whole number of 8-byte units | NOT DELIVERED | raises DESCRIPTOR_FAULT; the compiler reads such a box through the LSU |
| transposed `t.st.async` | NOT DELIVERED | mod[5] on a store raises DESCRIPTOR_FAULT |
| transposed transfer (`t.ld.async` mod[5]) | PROFILE-GATED | implemented behind HAS_TENSOR_XPOSE (profile core-xpose-v1, capability `tensor_transpose`): 16-bit elements, 4/8/16 source rows (ISA sec 9E; tb/core/progs/t30_xpose.s). Without it the encoding raises ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (t31_xpose_illegal.s) |
| 1-byte transposed transfer (`t.ld.async.b.t`) | PROFILE-GATED | R41 X8: HAS_TENSOR_XPOSE=2 (profile core-vrf-sync-v5-x8, capability `tensor_transpose_8bit`): int8/e4m3/e5m2, 4/8/16 source rows (tb/core/progs/t33_xpose8.s). A 16-bit-only engine raises DESCRIPTOR_FAULT (t34_xpose8_old.s) |
| general CFG in the MLIR verifier | FROZEN BOUNDARY | refused by name (IR-02), not accepted unchecked |
| `tnca_vector_fpu` synthesis | NOT COMPLETED | see `doc/synthesis.md`; yosys did not finish |
